title: Status sets and the project's statuses
summary: Every object, sheet, document and task has a status from a status set: the five categories New, Active, Resolved, Closed and Removed, with sub-statuses a set adds under them. Configuration → Statuses makes a set and chooses the one each level reads.
roles: Seeing statuses: everyone who can view the project. Making a project's status set and choosing the sets: Manage project workflows (Project administrator); a company set: Edit the company library

title: The status chip: set an item's status
summary: Under an object's name the status chip shows its status (its category before it when they differ), HOLD, and No workflow. Click it to set another status of its set.
roles: Setting a status: Move items in their workflow (Engineer and above)

title: Value statuses: Assumed, Preliminary, Confirmed, Final
summary: A value carries a status of its own, set from its row's right-click menu and shown by a mark after its name. A Confirmed or Final value that changes becomes Preliminary again. Calculated values have none.
roles: Set value statuses (Engineer and above) and edit attributes

title: Put an item or a value on hold
summary: Put on hold… with a reason marks an object, a sheet, a document or one value HOLD, with who and why; Release hold takes it off. A hold never blocks editing; it is a filter and a column in the query view.
roles: Put on hold (Lead engineer, Project administrator)

title: Workflows: steps an item moves through
summary: A workflow is the statuses of a status set in order, its steps, with a credit, a time limit and a lock each may have. Make one from a template (Engineering deliverable, ISO 19650 deliverable, Instrument data, Diagram, Engineering object) in Configuration → Workflows.
roles: Making a project's workflow: Manage project workflows (Project administrator); a company workflow: Edit the company library

title: Assign workflows and start them
summary: Assignments say which workflow the project's items follow: objects by class (then their parent classes, then any class), sheets, documents, tasks. Apply starts the workflow on every item that has not started it, as one change.

title: Move an item to another step
summary: On the status chip an item with a workflow moves: to the next step, back to an earlier one with a reason, to Removed and back with a reason. A held item does not move forward; in a locked step its values, name and tag wait until it is moved back.
roles: Move items in their workflow (Engineer and above)

title: The workflow board
summary: A workflow's items as cards in a column per step and Removed, with their days in the step, returns and HOLD. Drag a card to another column, or use Move to… on it, to move it.
roles: Seeing the board: everyone who can view the project; moving cards: Move items in their workflow

title: Exit criteria: what an item needs before it moves on
summary: A step may say what an item needs before it moves on: required values filled in, values confirmed and not on hold, related items far enough, no open errors, a revision issued, a checklist ticked, a condition. The status chip lists them with ticks and crosses; an item whose criteria all pass shows Ready to move.
roles: Seeing criteria: everyone who can view the project; ticking a checklist: Move items in their workflow

title: Approvals: sign or reject a step
summary: A step with an approval moves on only by its signatures: each sign-off step (Checked, Approved) is signed by someone who did not move the item into it, or sign an earlier step it names. A rejection with a reason sends the item back. An item changed after its approval shows Changed since Approved.
roles: Sign workflow approvals (Engineer and above, Reviewer), with a fresh sign-in

title: Override failing criteria
summary: With Override workflow checks, Override… moves an item on although a blocking criterion fails, with a reason that is kept with the item's step and in its history. An approval cannot be overridden.
roles: Override workflow checks (Lead engineer, Project administrator)

title: The flow: paths between steps
summary: Flow shows a workflow's steps in order with their credit, lock, criteria and approval, and its paths above them: extra moves such as Skip check (small change), each with an optional condition on the item. Add path… adds one and publishes a new version.

title: New workflow versions in a project
summary: A new version of a workflow reaches items from their next move. When it no longer has a status some items are in, Workflow updates lists them: map that status to a step, then Take version n moves them there as one change.

title: Dashboards: the project's and the environment's progress
summary: Dashboards on the left rail shows the project's dashboards and the environment's. Project progress, Data completeness and Review and comments are there from the start; Environment overview counts every project you may open.
roles: Everyone who can view the project, and is in a dashboard's audience

title: Tiles: numbers, bars and the items behind them
summary: A tile counts or measures the rows of a source (objects, sheets, required values, value statuses, workflow items, tasks, documents, markups, findings, projects), grouped or not. Click a number or a bar to list its items and open one.

title: Change a dashboard
summary: Edit changes the name and the tiles: add one from the catalogue, remove one, Save. Each save is a version; Versions lists the last 20 and restores one.
roles: A project dashboard: Manage project dashboards (Lead engineer, Project administrator); the organization's: Manage organization dashboards

title: Who sees a dashboard
summary: Who sees it: everyone in the project, Lead engineers or Project administrators. Show in E1 Reviewer offers the dashboard on the iPad.

title: Every-project dashboards
summary: A dashboard the organization makes for every project shows in each project with that project's data. Copy to this project makes it the project's own; Reset to the organization's brings the shared one back.
roles: Making one: Manage organization dashboards; copying and resetting: Manage project dashboards

title: Present a dashboard
summary: Present hides the controls and enlarges the tiles for a meeting; Stop presenting brings them back.
